region: Northern Uppland, on the river below Lake Tämnaren
description: Forsby sits where the river drops over a shelf of granite in a run of white rapids before it spreads out across the Uppland plain. The rapids have turned a grain mill for three hundred years and, since 1866, a water-driven saw belonging to a timber firm in Gävle. Around them lie a dozen farms in a straggling row village, the parish church on its gravel ridge, a posting inn on the Gävle road, and spruce forest closing in on three sides.
seasonNotes: October. The harvest is in and the flails thump in the threshing barns from dawn; every farm wants its flour ground before the roads turn to mire, so carts queue at the mill. The days shorten fast: brass-coloured light at four, dark by six. Frost whitens the stubble at dawn, then days of rain blow in from the west and the river runs high and brown. Pig slaughter begins at the month's end, and the smell of singed bristle hangs over the yards.
travel: From the Society's headquarters by cart to Uppsala, then by hired coach or post-carriage north on the Gävle road to Forsby, about seven hours with a change of horses at the halfway posting station (alternatively by rail to Stockholm, coastal steamer to Gävle, then south by carriage, much longer; the Uppsala-Gävle railway opens only in 1874).

geography.parish: Forsby parish, in the Tämnaren district
knownFor: Its rapids, which have driven a grain mill for three hundred years and now drive a company saw as well, a standing quarrel over water that the Uppland newspapers like to print
The Gävle road, the old post road north from Uppsala, with its posting inns, drovers and carters, and the unbuilt railway that is expected to replace it
Spruce forest and the Tämnaren river country, where timber and charcoal are floated or hauled to the old ironworks near the Dalälven coast
A farming parish drained by emigration, whose farms are being bought up by timber firms

neighbours.name: Tierp
neighbours.kind: market village and crown sheriff's seat
neighbours.distance: about 15 km north-northeast by the Gävle road, two hours by cart
offers: Small weekly trade and a seasonal market
Post and carriers for the Gävle road
Railway station from 1874 (Uppsala-Gävle line, now under survey and construction)

neighbours.name: Uppsala
neighbours.distance: about 50 km south by the Gävle road, seven hours by post-carriage
offers: Upsala Sparbank and Uplands Enskilda Bank
The Society's headquarters lie just outside the town

neighbours.name: Gävle
neighbours.distance: about 75 km north by road, a long day by carriage
offers: Seat of the timber company that owns the saw
Harbour with the Stockholm-Härnösand coastal steamer in the open season

neighbours.name: Örbyhus
neighbours.distance: about 20 km northeast by country road
offers: Road connections to Tierp and Gävle
Station on the future railway, from 1874

authorities.police: Crown sheriff (kronolänsman) of the Tämnaren and river district, seated at Tierp, about 15 km off. In Forsby itself the only law is the parish constable (fjärdingsman), a farmer chosen for the post, and the parish meeting.
authorities.court: District court (häradsrätt) for the Tämnaren district, seated at Uppsala, about 50 km away. The judge (häradshövding) and twelve lay assessors sit at fixed sessions a few times a year, and the autumn session is normally held after harvest.
authorities.doctor: Provincial doctor for northern Uppland, seated at Tierp, about 15 km off. He covers a wide district, so a call to Forsby may take a day or more, and he is often summoned to the mill and the saw.
authorities.post: The post goes by the Gävle road. Letters are left at the posting inn, and a carrier from Tierp calls about twice a week. The Gävle road post-carriages pass daily, and parcels or urgent letters can be put on one at a cost.
authorities.telegraph: None at Forsby or Tierp. The nearest office is at Uppsala, about 50 km south, and another at Gävle, about 75 km north. A telegram must be taken there by rider or carriage.
authorities.bank: Upsala Sparbank and Uplands Enskilda Bank, both at Uppsala, about 50 km. The mill and the saw deal with the Gävle banks and the timber company's head office.
authorities.newspaper: Upsala, from Uppsala. A Gävle paper also reaches the inn a day or two late, and the vicar and the inn-keeper take it.

routes.name: By road: Gävle road post-carriage (the usual way)

legs.to: halfway posting station on the Gävle road
legs.cost: about 3 to 4 riksdaler for a carriage and pair, plus the driver's tip
legs.schedule: post-carriages and hired carriages leave all day; order horses at the post station, and in autumn book ahead for harvest and market traffic
legs.notes: The road runs north through farmland and forest strips. The first change of horses is at the halfway station, where the inn serves coffee and rye bread. In October heavy rain makes the clay stretches slow.

legs.from: halfway posting station on the Gävle road
legs.cost: about 3 to 4 riksdaler for the second stage
legs.schedule: fresh horses at the halfway station; the last stage should leave by early afternoon to arrive before dark
legs.notes: A side road off the Gävle road leads down to the river, and the sound of the rapids carries long before the village appears. Seven hours in all, with the change. The railway is only a survey so far: rail to Tierp from 1874.

routes.name: By rail and coastal steamer, then road (long, only if the Gävle road is flooded or blocked)

legs.notes: The railway opened in 1866 and is the only line that runs from Uppsala. From the Stockholm terminus take a cab to the harbour.

legs.duration: about 20 to 24 hours with calls on the coast
legs.cost: about 6 to 10 riksdaler for a berth
legs.schedule: sails a few times a week in the open season, and the last sailings of the year are in October
legs.notes: Late-season gales and fog can delay or cancel sailings, and the steamer stops at Östhammar on the way. This detour takes you far past Forsby, so use it only if the road is closed.

legs.cost: about 6 to 8 riksdaler for a carriage and pair for the day
legs.schedule: hire at the Gävle inns; set out early
legs.notes: The same Gävle road run in the opposite direction, south by Örbyhus and Tierp. The Uppsala-Gävle railway is not open until 1874, so there is no train on this stretch.

journey.journeyScene: The Gävle road runs out of Uppsala between wet stubble fields, and the carriage wheels throw up brown water from every rut. At the halfway station the postmaster's wife puts coffee on the table while the horses are changed, and the stable-lad says the river has been loud this week. Past the last farms the spruce closes in on both sides, the light fades early in October, and from far ahead comes a low steady roar of water over granite. Lamps are lit in the posting inn at Forsby long before you see the mill and the saw crouched beside the rapids..

publicFacts: The grain mill has belonged to the Ers family for four generations; the present miller is a widower with two grown sons.
The sawmill below the rapids is owned by a timber company in Gävle, which bought the water rights in 1866 after a long quarrel with the village.
In dry summers the saw and the grain mill compete for water, and the parish meeting has twice had to rule on who may open the sluice first.
Three Forsby families left for America this spring; their farms were sold at auction and bought by the sawmill company.
A lay preacher of the revival holds meetings in a farmhouse kitchen on Sunday afternoons, which the vicar has spoken against from the pulpit.
The vicar's household examinations begin in the first week of November, farm by farm.
Surveyors' pegs for the coming railway run across the fields east of the village.

places.name: Forsby Mill
places.ownerRole: the miller, whose family has owned the mill for generations
places.description: The mill stands on the rock at the head of the rapids, its timber walls grey and furred with flour dust. The great wheel turns with a heavy wet thud you feel through the floorboards, and spray from the race hangs in the cold air. Inside, the stones grumble and the room is warm and smells of meal and wet wood. Farm carts wait in the yard in the drizzle, their horses steaming under sacking.

affordances.name: Waterwheel and race
affordances.description: An overshot wheel twice a man's height, green with weed, fed by a timber race from the dam.

affordances.name: Mill pond
affordances.description: The dammed reach above the rapids, wide and slate-coloured, with the sluice gate the whole village argues over.

affordances.name: Millstones
affordances.description: The stones, hopper and gearing, everything white with meal.

affordances.name: Grain loft
affordances.description: The loft where sacks wait to be ground.

affordances.name: Mill store
affordances.description: A store of spare cogs, pick-hammers for dressing the stones and sacks.

affordances.name: Miller's house
affordances.description: The miller's cottage beside the mill, with its own hearth.

contains.name: Hearth
contains.description: The miller's hearth.

affordances.name: Mill office
affordances.description: A small office where the miller keeps his tallies of grain and toll.

contains.name: Locked drawer

places.name: The Company Saw
places.ownerRole: the foreman who runs the saw for a Gävle timber company
places.description: Below the rapids the company saw shrieks from first light, two frame saws rising and falling in an open-sided hall. Sawdust drifts on the water and lies in yellow banks along the shore, sodden with rain. Rafts of logs jostle in the boom, and the sawyers, most of them hired from Hälsingland, shout over the noise in their own dialect. Stacks of fresh planks smell sharply of resin.

affordances.name: Saw wheel and race
affordances.description: The wheel and race that drive the frame saw.

affordances.name: Log pond
affordances.description: A boomed backwater of the river packed with floated logs, slick and dark, that men walk across with pike poles.

affordances.name: Saw hall
affordances.description: The saw hall: frame saws rising and falling, the floor ankle-deep in sawdust.

affordances.name: Timber yard
affordances.description: Stacked planks in rows to dry, roofed with boards.

affordances.name: Filing shed
affordances.description: Where the saw-filer sharpens blades among files and setting tools.

affordances.name: Workers' barracks
affordances.description: A barracks of bunks for the saw hands, damp clothes on lines across the room.

affordances.name: Sawmill office
affordances.description: The company office with the ledgers, timber measures and wage lists.

contains.name: Clerk's desk
contains.description: A clerk's sloping desk with the timber tally.

contains.name: Locked drawer
contains.description: A locked drawer with contracts and letters from the timber merchants.

contains.name: Wage box
contains.description: An iron box holding the fortnight's wages.

affordances.name: Sawyers' cottages
affordances.description: Three company cottages on the bank below the saw, each shared by two families of sawyers and log drivers.

places.name: Storgården
places.ownerRole: the village's largest freeholder farming family
places.description: The biggest farm in Forsby is a red-painted two-storey house, its windows framed in white, facing a yard of mud churned by carts. Threshing goes on in the barn with the flails beating in pairs, and chaff blows out of the door in gusts. A dog on a chain watches every stranger. Beyond the outbuildings the stubble fields run down, wet and silver, to the river.

affordances.name: Farmyard
affordances.description: The yard between the buildings, trodden mud and a woodpile.

affordances.name: Main room
affordances.description: The everyday room: open hearth, long table, wall beds and the loom in the corner.

contains.name: Open hearth
contains.description: The whitewashed corner hearth with its iron pot-hook.

affordances.name: Best room
affordances.description: The cold best room, painted furniture, the family Bible and a clock from Mora.

contains.name: Dowry chest
contains.description: A painted chest with the wife's linen and the year of her wedding on the lid.

affordances.name: Farmhands' chamber
affordances.description: A bare chamber with two beds and the hands' own chests.

affordances.name: Cowshed
affordances.description: A low dark byre, warm with cattle breath.

affordances.name: Stable
affordances.description: A stable for the farm horse or horses.

affordances.name: Barn
affordances.description: A timber barn for the harvest.

contains.name: Hayloft
contains.description: The hay store over the barn floor, reached by a ladder.

affordances.name: Threshing barn
affordances.description: A threshing barn (loge) where the grain is threshed with flails through the autumn.

affordances.name: Root cellar
affordances.description: A root cellar dug into the slope, holding potatoes, turnips and the milk.

affordances.name: Well
affordances.description: A well with a sweep pole and a wooden bucket.

affordances.name: Bathhouse
affordances.description: A small log bastu with a stone oven, also used for drying malt and flax.

places.name: Forsby Church
places.description: The medieval church sits on the gravel ridge above the village, whitewashed walls streaked grey by the rain. A separate tarred bell frame stands beside it, and the churchyard birches have dropped their leaves in yellow drifts on the graves. Inside it is colder than outdoors and smells of damp stone and tallow. Painted saints in faded red and ochre look down from the vaults.

affordances.name: Sacristy
affordances.description: A small vaulted room off the chancel where the vicar robes.

contains.name: Vestment cupboard
contains.description: A tall cupboard of chasubles, the surplice and spare altar candles.

contains.name: Parish chest
contains.description: An ancient iron-banded chest with three locks for the communion silver and old deeds.

affordances.name: Bell tower
affordances.description: Steep ladders up to the bells, bird droppings on the beams, wind through the louvres.

affordances.name: Church loft
affordances.description: The dusty space above the vaults, full of broken pews and old hatchments.

affordances.name: Burial vault
affordances.description: A brick-lined vault under the chancel floor where a landed family lay their coffins.

places.name: Forsby Posting Inn
places.ownerRole: the keeper of the posting inn
places.description: The posting inn stands where the Gävle road crosses the river, a long low house with a lantern burning by the door from mid-afternoon. In the taproom the stove ticks and travellers' coats steam on pegs, and the landlady keeps coffee on the boil. The posting horses stamp in the stable across the yard. The posting book lies open on a shelf for every traveller to sign.

affordances.name: Taproom
affordances.description: The public room: benches, a long scrubbed table, a tiled stove and the day's travellers.

affordances.name: Kitchen
affordances.description: A smoky kitchen with an open hearth, copper pans and a bread rack under the ceiling.

contains.name: Pantry
contains.description: A cold larder of salted meat, cheeses, crispbread and the brännvin keg.

affordances.name: Guest room 1
affordances.description: A narrow room with a bed, a washstand and a window onto the yard.

contains.name: Travelling chest
contains.description: A painted chest at the foot of the bed for a guest's things.

affordances.name: Guest room 2
affordances.description: A narrow room with a bed, a washstand and a window onto the yard.

contains.name: Travelling chest
contains.description: A painted chest at the foot of the bed for a guest's things.

affordances.name: Posting stable
affordances.description: Stalls for the posting horses, harness on pegs, the smell of hay and dung.

affordances.name: Cellar
affordances.description: A stone cellar for ale, potatoes and the inn's barrels.

affordances.name: Landlord's office
affordances.description: A cramped room with the posting book, receipts on a spike and a calendar from a Stockholm brewer.

contains.name: Writing desk
contains.description: A writing desk of stained pine with pigeonholes for letters.

contains.name: Locked drawer
contains.description: A drawer under the writing flap, fitted with a small iron lock.

contains.name: Strongbox
contains.description: An iron-bound strongbox bolted to the floor, holding the takings.

places.name: The Smithy at the Bridge
places.description: The smithy is a soot-black log house by the bridge, its door open to let out the heat, so the forge glows orange against the grey afternoon. The ring of the hammer carries across the water. A horse waits patiently to be shod, tied to a ring in the wall. Inside it smells of hot iron, coal and singed hoof.

affordances.name: Forge
affordances.description: The hearth and bellows, the anvil on its stump, the quench trough.

affordances.name: Workshop
affordances.description: The bench and racks of tongs, hammers and half-finished work.

affordances.name: Coal shed
affordances.description: A shed of charcoal and bar iron from the works.

affordances.name: Smith's cottage
affordances.description: The smith's one-room cottage across the yard.

contains.name: Smith's chest
contains.description: The smith's own chest of papers and good clothes.

places.name: Granbacken
places.ownerRole: a crofter family on the farm's land
places.description: A grey one-room croft stands at the forest edge on a stony slope a mile above the village, its turf roof sprouting withered grass. Smoke leaks from the chimney and the potato patch is dug over and black. The spruce stand dark and dripping just behind the byre. A path of roots and stones leads down through the trees to the river.

affordances.name: Cottage room
affordances.description: One room: hearth, a box bed for the parents, a pull-out bench for the children, a table under the window.

contains.name: Hearth
contains.description: The hearth, smoke-blackened, a pot simmering.

contains.name: Clothes chest
contains.description: The family's one chest for Sunday clothes and papers.

contains.name: Loose board
contains.description: A loose floorboard by the bed where a few coins can be kept.

affordances.name: Byre
affordances.description: A byre built against the cottage for one cow and a few sheep.

affordances.name: Earth cellar
affordances.description: A turf-roofed earth cellar for potatoes.

affordances.name: Well
affordances.description: A shallow well or a spring-fed pit with a bucket.

affordances.name: Potato patch
affordances.description: A stony patch of potatoes, kale and tobacco plants.
